text:
If $\int \frac{\cos x-\sin x}{\sqrt{8-\sin 2x}}dx=a\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{\sin x+\cos x}{b}\right )+c$, where c is a constant of integration, then
the ordered pair (a, b) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $\int \frac{\cos x-\sin x}{\sqrt{8-\sin 2x}}dx$

Write sin2x = 1 + sin2x - 1

= $\int \frac{\cos x-\sin x}{\sqrt{8-[1+\sin 2x-1]}}dx$

= $\int \frac{\cos x-\sin x}{\sqrt{8-\left [\sin ^{2}x+\cos ^{2}x+2\sin x\cos x-1\right ]}}dx$

= $\int \frac{\cos x-\sin x}{\sqrt{8-\left [(\sin x+\cos x)^{2}-1\right ]}}dx$

= $\int \frac{\cos x-\sin x}{\sqrt{9-(\sin x+\cos x)^{2}}}dx$

put sin x + cos x = t

$\Rightarrow$ (cos x – sin x) dx = dt

= $\int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{9-(t)^{2}}}$

= $\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{t}{3}\right )$ + C

= $\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{\sin x+\cos x}{3}\right )+C$

$\therefore$ a = 1 and b = 3
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text:
If f : R $\to$ R is a function defined by f(x)= [x - 1] $\cos \left (\frac{2x-1}{2}\right )π$, where [.] denotes the greatest
integer function, then f is :
options: discontinuous at all integral values of x except at x = 1
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $f(x)=[x-1]\cos \left (\frac{2x-1}{2}\right )π$ where [ . ] is greatest integer function and f : R $\to$ R

$\because$ It is a greatest integer function then we need to check its continuity at x $\in$ I except these it is continuous.

Let, x = n where n $\in$ I

Then 

LHL = $\lim _{x\to n^{-}}[x-1]\cos \left (\frac{2x-1}{2}\right )π$

$=(n-2)\cos \left (\frac{2x-1}{2}\right )π=0$

RHL = $\lim _{x\to n^{+}}[x-1]\cos \left (\frac{2x-1}{2}\right )π$

$=(n-1)\cos \left (\frac{2x-1}{2}\right )π=0$

and f(n) = 0

Here, $\lim _{x\to n^{-}}f(x)=\lim _{x\to n^{+}}f(x)=f(n)$

$\therefore$ It is continuous at every integers.

Therefore, the given function is continuous for all real x.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text:
The function 

f(x) = $\frac{4x^{3}-3x^{2}}{6}-2\sin x+(2x-1)\cos x$ :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $f(x)=\frac{4x^{3}-3x^{2}}{6}-2\sin x+(2x-1)\cos x$

$f^{'}(x)=\frac{12x^{2}-6x}{6}-2\cos x+(2x-1)(-\sin x)+\cos x(2)$

$=(2x^{2}-x)-2\cos x-2x\sin x+\sin x+2\cos x$

$=2x^{2}-x-2x\sin x+\sin x$

$=2x(x-\sin x)-1(x-\sin x)$

$f^{'}(x)=(2x-1)(x-\sin x)$

for $x>0,x-\sin x>0$

$x<0,x-\sin x<0$

for $x\in (-\infty ,0]\cup \left [\frac{1}{2},\infty \right ),f^{'}(x)\geq 0$

for $x\in \left [0,\frac{1}{2}\right ],f^{'}(x)\leq 0$

Hence, f(x) increases in $\left [\frac{1}{2},\infty \right )$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}\frac{\int\limits _{0}^{x2}\sin (\sqrt{t})dt}{x^{3}}$

This is in $\frac{0}{0}$ form, so use L' Hospital rule

$=\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}\frac{\frac{d}{dx}\left (\int\limits _{0}^{x2}\sin (\sqrt{t})dt\right )}{\frac{d}{dx}(x^{3})}$

$=\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}\frac{\sin x.2x-0}{3x^{2}}$

(applying Leibnitz rule)

$=\frac{2}{3}\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}\frac{\sin x}{x}$

$=\frac{2}{3}$

text:
A man is walking on a straight line. The arithmetic mean
of the reciprocals of the intercepts of this line on the
coordinate axes is $\frac{1}{4}$. Three stones A, B and C are placed at the points
(1, 1), (2, 2) and (4, 4) respectively. Then, which of these stones is / are on the path of the man?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Given, position of A = (1, 1)

Position of B = (2, 2)

Position of C = (4, 4)


[IMG]

Let x-intercept be a and y-intercept be b.

Equation of line traced is

$\frac{x}{a}+\frac{y}{b}=1$

This is the equation of path, let a point (h, k) lie on this path.

Then, $\frac{h}{a}+\frac{k}{b}=1$

Also, AM of reciprocal of a and b = $\frac{1}{4}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}}{2}=\frac{1}{4}$

$\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}=\frac{1}{2}$

On comparing Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get (h, k) = (2, 2)

Hence, the required stone is B(2, 2).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text:
Let p and q be two numbers such that p + q = 2 and $p^{4}+q^{4} = 272$. Then p and q are
roots of the equation :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$p^{2}+q^{2}=(p+q)^{2}-2pq$

$=4-2pq$

Now, $\left (p^{2}+q^{2}\right )^{2}=p^{4}+q^{4}+2p^{2}q^{2}$

$\Rightarrow (4-2pq)^{2}=272+2p^{2}q^{2}$

$\Rightarrow 16+4p^{2}q^{2}-16pq=272+2p^{2}q^{2}$

$\Rightarrow 2p^{2}q^{2}-16pq-256=0$

$\Rightarrow p^{2}q^{2}-8pq-128=0$

$\Rightarrow (pq-16)(pq+8)=0$

$\Rightarrow pq=16,-8$

Here, pq = - 8 gives the equation $x^{2}-2x-8=0$, which is not among the options.

$\therefore$ pq = 16, for which p and q are non-real.

Now, the equation whose roots are p and q is

$x^{2}-2x+16=0$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text:
The area (in sq. units) of the part of the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} = 36$, which is outside the parabola
$y^{2} = 9x$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]
 
$x^{2}+y^{2}=36$ and $y^{2}=9x$

$\therefore$ $x^{2}+9x-36=0$

$\Rightarrow x=3,-12$

Required Area, 

$A=π(6)^{2}-2[A_{1}+A_{2}]$

$A=π(6)^{2}-2\left [\int\limits _{0}^{3}\sqrt{9x}dx+\int\limits _{3}^{6}\sqrt{36-x^{2}}dx\right ]$

$=36π-2\left [\left [3\times \frac{2}{3}x^{\frac{3}{2}}\right ]_{0}^{3}+\left [\frac{x}{2}\sqrt{36-x^{2}}+\frac{36}{2}\sin ^{-1}\frac{x}{6}\right ]_{3}^{6}\right ]$

$=36π-2\left [\left [2x^{\frac{3}{2}}\right ]_{0}^{3}+\left [\frac{x}{2}\sqrt{36-x^{2}}+18\sin ^{-1}\frac{x}{6}\right ]_{3}^{6}\right ]$

$=36π-2\left [\left [6\sqrt{3}-0\right ]+\left [\left (0+18\sin ^{-1}\frac{6}{6}\right )-\left (\frac{3}{2}\times 3\sqrt{3}+18\sin ^{-1}\frac{3}{6}\right )\right ]\right ]$

$=36π-2\left [\left [6\sqrt{3}\right ]+\left [\left (\frac{18π}{2}\right )-\left (\frac{3}{2}\times 3\sqrt{3}+\frac{18π}{6}\right )\right ]\right ]$

$=36π-$ $\left (12\sqrt{3}+18π-9\sqrt{3}-6π\right )$

= $24π-3\sqrt{3}$

Note :

(i) $\int \sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}dx=\frac{1}{2}\left [x\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}+a^{2}\log |x+\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}|\right ]+C$

(ii) $\int \sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}dx=\frac{1}{2}\left [x\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}+a^{2}\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{x}{a}\right )\right ]+C$

(iii) $\int \sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}dx=\frac{1}{2}\left [x\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}-a^{2}\log |x+\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}|\right ]+C$

satisfies the equation $t^{2} - 9t + 8 = 0$, then the value of

$\frac{2\sin x}{\sin x+\sqrt{3}\cos x}\left (0<x<\frac{π}{2}\right )$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$e^{(\cos ^{2}x+\cos ^{4}x+...........\infty )\ln 2}=2^{\cos ^{2}x+\cos ^{4}x+...........\infty }$

= $2^{\frac{\cos 2x}{1-\cos 2x}}$

$=2^{\cot ^{2}x}$

Given, $t^{2}-9t+8=0\Rightarrow t=1,8$

$\Rightarrow 2^{\cot ^{2}x}=1,8\Rightarrow \cot ^{2}x=0,3$

$0<x<\frac{π}{2}\Rightarrow \cot x=\sqrt{3}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{2\sin x}{\sin x+\sqrt{3}\cos x}=\frac{2}{1+\sqrt{3}\cot x}=\frac{2}{4}=\frac{1}{2}$

text:
The locus of the mid-point of the line segment joining the focus of the parabola $y^{2} = 4ax$ to a
moving point of the parabola, is another parabola whose directrix is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, equation of parabola $\Rightarrow$ $y^{2} = 4ax$

Focus = S(a, 0)

Let any point on the parabola be P(at$^{2}, 2at)$.


[IMG]

and let the mid-point of PS be M(h, k).

$\therefore$ $h=\frac{at^{2}+a}{2};k=\frac{2at+0}{2}$

$\Rightarrow t^{2}=\frac{2h-a}{a};t=\frac{k}{a}$

$\Rightarrow t^{2}=\frac{k^{2}}{a^{2}}$

Now, $\frac{2h-a}{a}=\frac{k^{2}}{a^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow 2h-a=\frac{k^{2}}{a}\Rightarrow k^{2}=a(2h-a)$

$\therefore$ Locus of (h, k) is $y^{2}=a(2x-a)$

$y^{2}=2a\left (x-\frac{a}{2}\right )$

$\therefore$ The directrix of this parabola is 

$x-\frac{a}{2}=-\frac{a}{2}\Rightarrow x=0$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

3x - 2y - kz = 10

2x - 4y - 2z = 6

x+2y - z = 5m

is inconsistent if :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 3 & -2 & -k \\ 2 & -4 & -2 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \end{array}\right |=0$

$3(4+4)+2(-2+2)-k(4+4)=0$

$\Rightarrow k=3$

$\Delta _{x}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 10 & -2 & -3 \\ 6 & -4 & -2 \\ 5m & 2 & -1 \end{array}\right |\neq 0$

$10(4+4)+2(-6+10m)-3(12+20m)\neq 0$

$80-12+20m-36-60m\neq 0$

$40m\neq 32\Rightarrow m\neq \frac{4}{5}$

$\Delta _{y}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 3 & 10 & -3 \\ 2 & 6 & -2 \\ 1 & 5m & -1 \end{array}\right |\neq 0$

$3(-6+10m)-10(-2+2)-3(10m-6)\neq 0$

$-18+30m-30m+18\neq 0\Rightarrow 0$

$\Delta _{z}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} 3 & -2 & 10 \\ 2 & -4 & 6 \\ 1 & 2 & 5m \end{array}\right |\neq 0$

$3(-20m-12)+2(10m-6)+10(4+4)-40m+32\neq 0\Rightarrow m\neq \frac{4}{5}$

text:
Let P = $\left [\begin{array}{lll} 3 & -1 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & α \\ 3 & -5 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$, where $α$ $\in$ R. Suppose Q = [ $q_{ij}$] is a matrix satisfying $PQ = kI_{3}$ for some non-zero k $\in$ R. 
If $q_{23} =$ $-\frac{k}{8}$
and |Q| = $\frac{k^{2}}{2}$, then $α^{2}$ $+ k^{2}$ is equal to $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As $PQ=kI\Rightarrow Q=kP^{-1}I$

now $Q=\frac{k}{|P|}(adjP)I$

$\Rightarrow Q=\frac{k}{(20+12α)}\left [\begin{array}{lll} - & - & - \\ - & - & (-3α-4) \\ - & - & - \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

$\because$ $q_{23}=\frac{-k}{8}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{k}{(20+12α)}(-3α-4)=\frac{-k}{8}$

$\Rightarrow 2(3α+4)=5+3α$

$3α=-3\Rightarrow α=-1$

also $|Q|=\frac{k^{3}|I|}{|P|}\Rightarrow \frac{k^{2}}{2}=\frac{k^{3}}{(20+12α)}$

$\Rightarrow$ $(20+12α)=2k\Rightarrow 8=2k\Rightarrow k=4$

text: $\lim _{n\to \infty }\tan \left \{\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{1+r+r^{2}}\right )\right \}$ is equal to $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{1+r+r^{2}}\right )$

$=\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{r+1-r}{1+r(r+1)}\right )$

$=\tan ^{-1}(r+1)-\tan ^{-1}r$

$\therefore$ $\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}\left (\tan ^{-1}(r+1)-\tan ^{-1}(r)\right )$

$=\tan ^{-1}(2)-\tan ^{-1}(1)+\tan ^{-1}(3)-\tan ^{1}(2)+\tan ^{-1}(n+1)-\tan ^{-1}(n)$

$=\tan ^{-1}(n+1)-\tan ^{-1}(1)$

$=\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{n+1-1}{1+(n+1)1}\right )$

$=\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{n}{n+2}\right )$

$\lim _{n\to \infty }\tan \left (\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{1+r+r^{2}}\right )\right )$

$=\lim _{x\to \infty }\tan \left (\tan ^{-1}\left (\frac{n}{n+2}\right )\right )$

$=\lim _{x\to \infty }\frac{n}{n+2}$

$=1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In this problem, we're dealing with 3-digit numbers in set $A$, and subsets $B$ and $C$ which represent numbers of specific forms.

1. First, we consider the numbers of the form $9k+2$ (Set $B$) within the 3-digit range, which starts at 101 and ends at 992.

2. We calculate the sum of these numbers, denoted as $s_{1}$. To calculate $s_{1}$, you use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series : 

 

   $(n/2)\times (\text{first term}+\text{last term})$ 

 

  Here, $n$ is the total count of such numbers. These are 3-digit numbers of the form $9k+2$, and we can find the total count by subtracting the smallest such number (101) from the largest (992), dividing the result by 9 (because we're considering numbers with a difference of 9), and then adding 1.

  

 The sum $s_{1}$ is calculated as follows :

 

  $(100/2)\times (101+992)=54650$

3. According to the problem, the sum of all elements of the set $A\cap (B\cup C)$ is $274\times 400=109600$. 

 

  Since the set $A\cap (B\cup C)$ is the union of two disjoint sets (the set of all three-digit numbers of form $9k+2$ and the set of all three-digit numbers of form $9k+l$), we can write this sum as :

   $s_{1}$(for numbers of the form  9k + 2) + $s_{2}$  (for numbers of the form  9k + l) = 109600

4. Solving this equation for $s_{2}$ (the sum of numbers of the form $9k+l$), we get :

 

  $s_{2}=109600-s_{1}=109600-54650=54950$

5. The sum $s_{2}$ can be expressed as $(n/2)\times (\text{first term}+\text{last term})$, where $n$ is the count of numbers of the form $9k+l$. The first term here is the smallest 3-digit number of this form, which is $99+l$, and the last term is the largest such number, which is $990+l$.

 

  We equate this to $s_{2}$ to solve for $l$ :

   $54950=(100/2)[(99+l)+(990+l)]$

6. Simplifying this equation, we get :

 

  $2l+1089=1099$

 

  Solving for $l$, we find :

 

  $l=5$

So, the correct answer is 5.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift

text: If $\int\limits _{-a}^{a}(|x|+|x-2|)dx=22$, (a > 2) and [x] denotes the greatest integer $\leq$ x, then $\int\limits _{a}^{-a}(x+[x])dx$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 24th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int\limits _{-a}^{a}(|x|+|x-2|)dx=22$

$\Rightarrow$ $\int\limits _{-a}^{0}(-2x+2)dx+\int\limits _{0}^{2}(x+2-x)dx+\int\limits _{2}^{a}(2x-2)dx=22$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2}-2x|_{0}^{-a}+2x|_{0}^{2}+x^{2}-2x|_{2}^{a}=22$

$\Rightarrow$ $a^{2}+2a+4+a^{2}-2a-(4-4)=22$

$\Rightarrow$ $2a^{2}=18\Rightarrow a=3$

$\int\limits _{3}^{-3}(x+[x])dx=-\left (\int\limits _{-3}^{3}(x+[x])dx\right )=-\left (\int\limits _{-3}^{3}[x]dx\right )$

= -($\int\limits _{-3}^{-2}[x]dx+\int\limits _{-2}^{-1}[x]dx+\int\limits _{-1}^{0}[x]dx$

+ $\int\limits _{0}^{1}[x]dx+\int\limits _{1}^{2}[x]dx+\int\limits _{2}^{3}[x]dx$)

$=-(-3-2-1+0+1+2)=3$

text: Let M be any 3 $\times$ 3 matrix with entries from the set {0, 1, 2}. The maximum number of such matrices, for which the sum of diagonal elements of $M^{T}M$ is seven, is $________$.

solution.body:
$\left [\begin{array}{lll} a & b & c \\ d & e & f \\ g & h & i \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{lll} a & d & g \\ b & e & h \\ c & f & i \end{array}\right ]$

$a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}+d^{2}+e^{2}+f^{2}+g^{2}+h^{2}+i^{2}=7$

Case I : Seven (1's) and two (0's)

Number of such matrices = ${}^{9}C_{2}=36$

Case II : One (2) and three (1's) and five (0's)

Number of such matrices = $\frac{9!}{5!3!}=504$

$\therefore$ Total = 540

Let $B_{i} (i = 1, 2, 3)$ be three independent events in a sample space. The probability that only $B_{1}$ occur is $α$, only $B_{2}$ occurs is $β$ and only $B_{3}$ occurs is $γ$. Let p be the probability that none of the events $B_{i}$ occurs and these 4 probabilities satisfy the equations $(α-2β)p=αβ$ and $(β-3γ)p=2βγ$ (All the probabilities are assumed to lie in the interval (0, 1)).
 Then $\frac{P(B_{1})}{P(B_{3})}$ is equal to $________$.
